blocks.html:
The core rmapi (pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api, the rasenmaeher_api package) is the integration point of Deploy App: it owns the authoritative user and certificate state, exposes the operations the UI and operators drive, and — critically — calls out to every registered product integration API over mTLS when a user changes. This page describes that surface so you understand what a core change touches before you make one. For how the other side of the contract is implemented, see Build an Integration rather than re-reading it here.

What the core exposes

At a high level the core provides three things:

  • User CRUD and enrollment — invite codes, approving waiting users, and the certificate-backed identity lifecycle. The first-admin bootstrap (rasenmaeher_api addcode) and the operator flows in the Operate book all run through these endpoints.
  • Deploy App operations — promote / demote / delete of users, product listing, and the proxy that fronts product integration content (/api/v1/product/proxy/<short_name>/...).
  • The outbound callback contract — the calls the core makes to each product integration when a user is created, revoked, promoted, demoted, or updated.

For authoritative, versioned paths, request bodies, and response shapes, use the API reference (rendered from the core's OpenAPI spec). Do not hand-copy endpoint signatures into prose.

The mTLS callback contract

This is the contract that makes Deploy App extensible, and the part of the core you must not break casually. When a user changes, the core issues HTTP callbacks to each registered product integration API. As implemented by the reference integration pvarki/python-matrix-rmapi and scaffolded by pvarki/python-integration-template, the contract is:

Callback Meaning
POST /api/v1/users/created A new device certificate was created for a user.
POST /api/v1/users/revoked A user's device certificate was revoked.
POST /api/v1/users/promoted A user was promoted to admin in Deploy App.
POST /api/v1/users/demoted A user was demoted from admin.
PUT /api/v1/users/updated A user's callsign was updated.

blocks.html:
Authentication is mutual TLS. Per the Matrix integration's README.rst, every /api/v1/users/* endpoint requires a valid mTLS client certificate whose CN matches the RASENMAEHER service certificate (taken from the kraftwerk manifest); any other caller gets 403 Forbidden. The core presents that service certificate; the integration verifies it. When you change the core's callback behaviour, you change what every integration's usercrud.py receives.

Integrations are expected to be idempotent and tolerant: a target service may not be ready when a callback fires, so integrations log and return success rather than failing the core's operation (see the Matrix "Deferred queue" behaviour). Keep this in mind when changing retry, ordering, or error semantics in the core — integrations were written against the current behaviour.

In the other direction, each integration exposes a GET /api/v1/healthcheck and a product description endpoint (GET /api/v1/description/{language}, returning a ProductComponent from description.py) that the core consumes to render product cards and proxy content.
